Script: Mas Foulaquier sits at the northern edge of Pic Saint-Loup, in the Languedoc, on a striking terroir of limestone scree over red clay. Swiss transplant Pierre Jéquier and his wife Blandine Chauchat have farmed the estate biodynamically since the early 2000s, working with old vines and native yeasts and keeping intervention to a minimum. L'Oiseau Blanc blends five Mediterranean white grapes (Grenache Blanc, Grenache Gris, Bourboulenc, Rolle and Clairette), aged in wood and sandstone amphora. The result is textured and aromatic, moving between citrus, orchard fruit and a savoury touch of garrigue herbs, with a fresh, mineral finish that pairs beautifully with the richness of the ox terrine and the sweetness of the carrot.

A very fresh Riesling from the Mosel in Germany, a region renowned for this variety. Bright apple and citrus wrapped in floral aromas, with macerated hybrids adding body, texture and a little grip.

Du Grappin is made by Andrew and Emma Nielsen of Le Grappin, an Australian couple who set up shop in Beaune and became cult favourites for wines of real precision. This Mâcon-Villages comes from old-vine Chardonnay on the cool, limestone-rich slopes above Azé. It's fermented with native yeasts and aged on its lees in old barrels, so you get a creamy, textured palate of ripe peach and white blossom, but the acidity keeps it fresh and lemony on the finish. That mix of richness and tension is what makes it so good with scallops: it matches their natural sweetness and cuts through the butter.

Alquimia comes from Marjorie and Stéphane Gallet in Roussillon, who farm biodynamically on steep schist hillsides. It's a vin de voile, a white aged oxidatively, so think of the nutty, savoury side of Jura wine or a fino sherry, but from Macabeu and Grenache Gris. It's dry and complex, with roasted nut, dried apricot and a saline, slatey freshness underneath. That nuttiness picks up the sweet earthiness of the Jerusalem artichoke, and the wine's savoury depth matches the umami of the mushrooms and koji, while the acidity keeps the dish from feeling heavy.

Think Sauvignon Blanc without the gooseberry. Lees ageing gives some texture, but it stays very fresh, grassy and floral. Clean and bright without being harshly acidic, so it sits beautifully with fresh lettuce.

Dish detail: Tempura and pickled squash, with ricotta, mixed herbs and chilli crisp
Script: Pop Bianco comes from the legendary Radikon family estate in Oslavje, right on the border with Slovenia. As an orange wine, the white varieties spend time fermenting on their skins, imparting a delicate tannic grip alongside notes of dried apricot, orange peel and herbal tea. While traditional Radikon cuvées undergo extensive maceration, this bottling sees a gentler touch, keeping it vibrant, juicy and infinitely fresh. That subtle skin-contact structure slices cleanly through the crunchy tempura and smooth ricotta, while its bright, zesty acidity echoes the pickled squash and holds its own against the lingering heat of the chilli.

Dish detail: Pollack with sardine emulsion, borlotti beans and tomato
Script: Villo comes from Agricola Gili, an exciting young venture on the southwestern shore of Sicily launched by Ermanno Vella and Alice Marconcini. Farming near the seaside village of Torretta Granitola, their 30-year-old Grillo vines sit barely a kilometre from the water on red clay and sand over limestone. Half the harvest undergoes a week of skin contact before blending with direct-pressed juice, followed by seven months of maturation in neutral oak. It brings a bright, saline lift driven by citrus, white peach and Mediterranean herbs, balanced by a gentle textural grip. That coastal character is ideal for the pollack: its racy minerality cuts through the dish, while the subtle skin-contact structure harmonises with the rich sardine emulsion and creamy borlotti beans, leaving the tomato to highlight the wine's vibrant, sun-ripened freshness.

Garance comes from Domaine Montanet-Thoden, the same Vézelay family estate behind our Galerne. Valentin Montanet farms organically, and most of the Pinot Noir vines face south, which gives this cool-climate red generous ripeness. It's medium-bodied and high-toned, with juicy red fruit, a touch of spice and silky tannins. Its fresh, Pinot-driven acidity keeps it lifted, which suits the richness and gamey depth of the venison without overpowering it.

Bordeaux can be very big and heavy, but Matthieu Cosse farms with respect for the land and picks earlier, so the wine keeps its freshness and acidity. It's bold and spicy, with rich dark fruit and a touch of wild strawberry. Tannins this strong could be hard going, but the sweet, earthy depth of the beetroot softens them and brings out the dark fruit rather than the green, eucalyptus edge of the Cabernet Sauvignon.

Script: Banyuls Rimage comes from very steep slopes close to the coast, where the sea influence helps preserve freshness. In a warm climate, sugar in the grapes rises quickly while acidity drops, so that coastal freshness matters. Lovely tannin structure and not overly sweet. A family-run estate working everything by hand and with horses.

This is a Riesling Spätlese from Thorsten Melsheimer, who farms organically and biodynamically on the Mullay-Hofberg, a very steep slate hillside above the Mosel. It's a late-harvest wine with a gentle sweetness, but the acidity is bright and the finish stays clean and slatey. The sweetness suits the panna cotta, and the acidity cuts through the cream. The apple in the wine echoes the apple on the plate, and the basil brings out its herbal, citrusy side. Together with the toasted sesame, it makes the whole dish feel light.

A beautifully balanced sweet Tokaj that invites another sip with every taste. This multi-vintage cuvée combines the depth and nobility of Aszú with the brightness of late-harvest fruit, resulting in a wine that is indulgent yet remarkably light on its feet. The nose is expressive and layered, opening with candied orange peel, peach compote and baked pear, followed by acacia honey, vanilla, cinnamon and a touch of saffron. On the palate, lush sweetness is countered by vibrant natural acidity, giving precision and lift to the rich core. Apricot, quince and citrus marmalade unfold over a fine mineral backbone, leading to a long, silky finish marked by gentle botrytis spice and freshness. A modern, elegant expression of sweet Tokaj: generous, harmonious and dangerously drinkable.

Langhe Nebbiolo is often called a poor man's Barolo, but the style is quite different. It shows Nebbiolo's more feminine side, with lighter texture, softer tannins from shorter macerations and, above all, the variety's delightful aromas of flowers and red fruits. Principiano's wines are all about freshness and subtlety, and the value for money is top. Ferdinando Principiano is on the southern fringe of the Barolo zone and benefits from the biodiversity of the Alta Langhe wilderness beyond the dense Nebbiolo plantings, which helps keep the vineyard in balance. In 2003 he moved away from conventional production and has been rewarded with purity and drinkability. He uses wild yeast fermentation and organic methods, and minimises sulphur.

Note: Primario, Atelier Kramar 2022: steep hillsides, an 800-year-old grape, a small family winery run by an artist couple.
Script: A historically significant grape, with over 800 years of orange-wine tradition in the region. The grape juice is quite low in flavour compared with the skins, so macerating the skins gives a wine with much more flavour. Textural and fresh, and a great pairing for rich agnolotti thanks to the tannin from skin contact. The leek velouté works well too: the richness has a nice backbone from the body of the wine and the tannins.
An almost-forgotten, darker-skinned Muscat sub-variety, made here into an off-dry sparkling wonder. L'Archetipo works with ancient grains as well as wine, with sustainability at its core.
